intro: Learn to express obligation: tengo que (personal) and hay que (general).
b1.texto:
**Tener que** + infinitive says who has to do it:

- **tengo que** estudiar (I)
- **tienes que** estudiar (you)
- **tiene que** estudiar (he, she)

**Hay que** + infinitive expresses a general obligation and never changes: **hay que** llegar a las nueve.

Use **porque** to give a reason: estudio **porque** mañana hay un examen. **¿Por qué?** (two words, with an accent) asks «why?».
b2.f2.texto: Because there is an exam tomorrow.
b2.f3.texto: We have to arrive at nine.
b4.texto: **Tener que** changes with the person (**tengo que**, **tiene que**). **Hay que** never changes. An infinitive always follows both.
b4.e1.texto: In the library you have to speak quietly.
b5.f0.texto: Lucía has to study this afternoon.
b5.f1.texto: Tomorrow there is an exam at school.
b5.f2.texto: That is why she sits down in her room.
b5.f3.texto: She opens the notebook and reads carefully.
b5.f4.texto: Pablo does not have to study today.
b5.f5.texto: But at home dinner has to be prepared.
b5.f7.texto: Then they have dinner together in the kitchen.
b6.pregunta: Complete the sentence to say «I have to study».
b6.o1.refuerzo: «De» is not used in tengo que.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Ir a» expresses a plan; tener uses que.
b7.traduccion: Because there is an exam tomorrow.
b8.pregunta: Complete the general rule: one has to arrive at nine.
b8.o2.refuerzo: «Es que» is not the structure; it is hay que.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Correct: two words with an accent ask «why?».
b10.pregunta: Which sentence says «I have to study»?
b10.o0.refuerzo: «Hay que» is general: it names nobody.
b10.o1.refuerzo: Correct: «Tengo que» names the person: I.
b11.pregunta: Translate into Spanish: «I have to study.»
p.tengo que.consejo: Personal obligation: it changes (tengo, tienes, tiene) and takes an infinitive.
p.hay que.consejo: General obligation: it never changes and names nobody.
p.hay que.glosa: one has to, it is necessary
p.porque.consejo: One word, no accent: it gives a reason.
p.por qué.consejo: Two words with an accent: used in questions.
p.estudiar.consejo: Infinitive: it goes after tengo que.
p.el examen.consejo: Masculine noun: el examen, un examen.
p.mañana.consejo: It also means «morning»: here it is the day after today.
p.llegar.consejo: Infinitive: it goes after hay que.
